title: Hocking, Ludonarrative Dissonance in Bioshock (Click Nothing, 2007)
label: practitioner
claim: Hocking, who worked on Far Cry 2, argues BioShock's mechanics (seek power, harvest Little Sisters) reward self-interest while its story says help others; he calls this a dissonance between what it is about as a game and as a story. It is his own reaction, not player data. The post never defines the term (it appears only in the title) and says nothing about genre mental models, though it calls self-interest a standard value in single player games.

title: Hodent, The Gamer's Brain (CRC Press 2017), Google Books snippet
label: snippet
claim: The only retrievable text is a figure caption on Norman-style mental models (user's mental model, system image, developer's model). Chapter on memory is listed in the contents. Not verified: that the book says players bring a genre-specific mental model, or anything about idle games.

title: Oliver and Pelletier, The things we learned on Liberty Island (DiGRA 2005)
label: research
claim: Qualitative study comparing Deus Ex players who did or skipped the training level; examines how players transfer previous gaming experience to a new game. Concludes games should recognise previous gaming experience and notes implications for defining genres. No effect sizes in the abstract.

title: Furlough and Gillan 2018, mental models of League of Legends players (J. Cognitive Engineering and Decision Making)
label: research
claim: 158 players grouped by hours. Novice mental models follow everyday-language associations; journeymen organise concepts procedurally (actions and goals); experts add abstract links and subnetworks. Shows players' models of a game differ by experience, within one game; does not test genre transfer.

title: Just how expert are expert video-game players? (PLoS/PMC 2013)
label: research
claim: Review/study arguing recent experience is a poor proxy for expertise and self-report can miss past experience. Seen in a search snippet only.

title: Desurvire, Caplan, Toth, Using Heuristics to Evaluate the Playability of Games (CHI 2004)
label: guideline
claim: HEP: heuristics for game play, story, mechanics and usability, tested on one evolving design vs standard user testing. Search summaries say it was most useful for general early issues and needed generalising across genres. PDF fetch returned binary, so content is from summaries only.

title: Pecorella, Quest for Progress: the math of idle games (GDC Europe 2016)
label: practitioner
claim: Cites a Quantic Foundry survey of players of three idle games: top motivators completion and power; advises making growth visible. Conference talk, seen as snippet; no study of how idle games frame goals.

title: Mao, Cuz She is My Daughter: How Players Navigate Ludo-Narrative Dissonance (Chinese DiGRA 2024)
label: research
claim: Identity V case study from player actions, video comments and interviews; per search summary, stronger character attachment shapes how players handle mechanic/backstory clashes. Page had no abstract; PDF unreadable.

title: Keefer 2023 Drexel MA thesis, player perception of ludic and narrative content in four games
label: research
claim: Survey (effective n=359) of Stardew Valley, WoW, Outer Wilds, Bloodborne with open-ended answers, aimed at dissonance/consonance/resonance. Abstract reports no results; thesis PDF not read.
